english: Of-Good-Fame, the warrior, rose up in the night. He yoked two swift horses, crossed the river and came to the cow-stall of the enemy. There the herdsmen were sleeping. Wolves cried on the black hills. Then he drove the livestock out. But a dog heard him and howled, and the herdsmen woke. He spoke to them: Herdsmen, do not tremble! I do not want your blood; I want the cattle of your master. They pursued him, but they did not come near him; his two horses were swift. Then the moon lit up the path, and he drove it to the village. At dawn his heart was glad. His mother saw it and spoke: My child, the gods love you. Give a share to Dyeus!

english: At the ford two warriors were standing. Man-Minded asked: Who are you? I am Of-True-Fame, the son of a king. These cattle I led from your enclosure, and I shall not give them to you. Then Man-Minded said: Let us two fight here! May Father Sky look upon us! But Of-True-Fame said: Why should we two die at the water? I shall give you ten horses in exchange for them. Then Man-Minded took the horses; the two joined hands and swore an oath. Then the two went apart, and the cattle followed Of-True-Fame. Of-True-Fame looked at the water and laughed: I live, and horses are born again.

english: In the house of the clan chief the warriors divided the cattle. The chief took the first share, and he gave bulls to the young men. He who had guarded the enclosure, to him they gave two sheep. Then the young men praised him: Giver of good things, may your fame be imperishable! He said: Cattle are the fame of men. Whoever drives them from the enemy, may he receive his share. In the night they ate meat and drank mead, and an old man chanted a song. Then sleep came to the young men, and the fire grew cold.

english: At dawn a young herdsman ran to the house of the lord. Lord, thieves came in the night, and they drove off our livestock. I fled and came to you. The lord asked: Who are the thieves? Where did they lead it? The herdsman spoke: They were men of Ill-Famed; they led it toward the hills. Then the lord grasped a spear and called the kin: Let us pursue them with swift horses! The kin yoked horses, and the herdsman showed them the path. They ran along the path, and the dogs ran before them. Their spears flashed in the sun. Black birds cried over the path.

english: The warriors of Of-Goodly-Fame followed the tracks of the herd. Through the fields they ran. In the evening they caught sight of dust on a hill. Then Of-Goodly-Fame spoke: Friends, the thieves are few, and we are many. Let us not fear them! Then they climbed the hill, and the foes fled. There they set a fire and cooked meat. Then they drove the herd to the village and rejoiced. Of-Goodly-Fame cried: Nothing is missing! His friends laughed and praised him. That night they slept under the stars.

english: Of-Good-Race came to the house of Ill-Famed and said: Your men slew my brother. Give me a hundred cattle in exchange for him, or we shall come with spears. Ill-Famed answered: I owe you nothing. Your brother, a thief, entered my field. He stole my livestock, and he died. Of-Good-Race spoke: Then the gods will see the truth. He went away to his own people, and Ill-Famed trembled in his heart. In the morning his people led a hundred sheep to the house of Of-Good-Race. Of-Good-Race took them, and he did not come again with spears. A wise man takes sheep; he does not take blood.
